name: NFHS-5 District Fact Sheets (2019-21)
publisher: International Institute for Population Sciences (IIPS) / Ministry of Health & Family Welfare
license: unstated (GoI publication; data.gov.in copy carries GODL-India)
caveats: NO violence indicators at district level - 104 indicators, none matching violence/empowerment/bank/mobile/decisions
domestic violence sits in the NFHS state module (long-questionnaire subsample) so IIPS publishes it at state/UT level only
Phase-1 release covers 341 districts of ~707; full coverage needs the Phase-2 release too
district boundaries are 2019-21 vintage and differ from Census 2011 and from current districts
survey prevalence, NOT reported crime - never blend with NCRB counts
evidence: rchiips.org and dhsprogram.com were EGRESS_BLOCKED from this session. Both official URLs were recovered from fetched third-party provenance files (ujjwalks96/geodemographic-india-llm data/README.md names the data.gov.in resource 'NFHS-5 India Districts Factsheet Data (Provisional)' as an .xls, and rchiips.org/nfhs/districtfactsheet_NFHS-5.shtml as the alternative). The 104-indicator list and absence of violence indicators were verified through two independent mirrors (see civil-society-academic-pratapvardhan-nfhs5).
how_to_obtain: Open rchiips.org/nfhs/districtfactsheet_NFHS-5.shtml from an unblocked network, or download the data.gov.in resource 'NFHS-5 India Districts Factsheet Data (Provisional)' (.xls).
notes: The brief assumed this carried district-level violence prevalence. It does not. Use it for socio-economic context and denominators only.

name: NFHS-5 State/UT Fact Sheets - Gender Based Violence block (indicators 125-127)
caveats: experienced-crime prevalence, NOT reported crime
only 36 rows - useless for sub-state mapping
DV module administered to a subsample (state module), so standard errors are larger than headline indicators
parenthesised values in the factsheets flag unweighted-case warnings and must be preserved
NFHS-5 asks ever-married women 18-49; NFHS-4 asked 15-49, so the age base changed between rounds
evidence: Fetched nfhs_violence_reference.csv. Header: 'Indicators,sub indicators,NFHS-5 (2019-20),STATE/UT'. Section 'Gender Based Violence (age 18-49 years)' has exactly three sub-indicators per state/UT: ever experienced spousal violence; physical violence during any pregnancy; young women 18-29 who experienced sexual violence by age 18. Observed values: Bihar 40.6/1.9/7.1, Andhra Pradesh 28.8/3.5/3.8, Assam 26.6/2.2/7.4, Goa 6.0/0.9/1.6, A&N Islands 23.2/(0.0)/1.4. Indicator numbers 125/126/127 of 131 confirmed independently from kri6228/AnemiaFusionNet's printed indicator list. National figure 29.3% (NFHS-5) vs 31.2% (NFHS-4) confirmed from a fetched PIB ministerial reply text.
how_to_obtain: open-download
notes: The best-measured experienced-violence number in India, and the anchor for any under-registration comparison against NCRB.

name: NFHS / DHS India microdata - Individual Recode with domestic violence module
license: DHS Terms of Use - free registration, per-survey approval, NO redistribution of microdata (derived aggregates may be published)
caveats: district cells are small: the DV module goes to roughly one eligible woman per selected household within the state-module subsample - wide confidence intervals are unavoidable
must weight with the DV-specific weight d005, not the standard individual weight v005
district identifiers follow the survey's own district frame, which must be crosswalked to current districts and to Census 2011 codes
prevalence, not incidence; ever-experienced vs last-12-months are different questions and must not be conflated
covers intimate-partner and sexual violence only - not crime in general
evidence: dhsprogram.com was EGRESS_BLOCKED from this session. A fetched peer-provenance file (chitagni/eco6810-final-project-template, peer-samples/03_literacy_imr_descriptive.md) states 'no DHS microdata registration is required for our design', confirming registration is the normal gate for the microdata route. NFHS-4 and NFHS-5 district-representative design is established from the factsheet structure (district factsheets exist for ~700 districts).
how_to_obtain: Register at dhsprogram.com, state a research purpose, request the India Individual Recode (IR) files for NFHS-5 (2019-21) and NFHS-4 (2015-16). Tabulate the d1xx domestic-violence variables by district identifier weighting by d005/1000000. Publish estimate plus n and CI per district; suppress cells below a pre-declared threshold.
notes: HIGHEST-VALUE LEAD IN THIS DOSSIER. The only route to district-level victimisation prevalence for India. It is a computation, not a download - and it needs no OCR.

name: NFHS-4 Fact Sheets (2015-16) - spousal violence indicators 103/104
caveats: whether the NFHS-4 DISTRICT factsheet also carried indicators 103/104 is UNRESOLVED - evidence points both ways and must be settled by opening one district PDF
age base is 15-49 in NFHS-4 vs 18-49 in NFHS-5 - the two rounds are not directly comparable without restricting the base
survey prevalence, not reported crime
evidence: Fetched HindustanTimesLabs/women-empowerment-index/data/103.csv. Header 'state,indicator,legend_name,urban,rural,total,rank'; indicator 103 = 'Ever-married women who have ever experienced spousal violence (%)' for all 36 states/UTs with urban/rural/total and rank (Sikkim 2.6 rank 1, Karnataka 20.5, Maharashtra 21.4, Chandigarh 22.5). The repo README confirms NFHS-4 source and eight 'Women's Empowerment and Gender-Based Violence' indicators. District status unresolved: Rayyan-mohammed/aarogya-lens schema_inspect.txt shows a GBV block at column indices 104-106 alongside a 'District Names' column, but the same repo's nfhs4_integration.py filters to Area=='Total' at state level and warns 'True district-to-district trend comparison is therefore not possible.'
how_to_obtain: open-download
notes: Phase-2 action: fetch one NFHS-4 district factsheet using the URL pattern rchiips.org/nfhs/pdf/NFHS4/<CODE>_FactSheet.pdf (pattern seen in a fetched supplementary_urls.txt) and check for the GBV section.

name: National Family Health Survey 6 (NFHS-6)
caveats: publication status unconfirmed
assume violence indicators remain state-level until shown otherwise - the constraint is the questionnaire design, not the release schedule
evidence: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Family_Health_Survey (fetched 2026-09-19) lists six rounds and names 'NFHS-6 (2023-2024, latest)'. The article gives no sample sizes, no district-estimate statement and no domestic-violence module detail. One GitHub repo (zerobug-mohit/NFHS-Atlas) claims a dashboard covering 'NFHS-4/5/6 survey data across 640 districts and 131 indicators' - claim not verified.
how_to_obtain: Check rchiips.org/nfhs and mohfw.gov.in for the NFHS-6 release. The NFHS-6 interviewer's manual states which questionnaire version carries the DV module, which settles the geography question.
notes: Monitor. If NFHS-6 moved the DV module into the household/short questionnaire, district-level violence prevalence becomes directly publishable and this project's headline constraint disappears.

name: Status of Policing in India Report (SPIR)
publisher: Common Cause with Lokniti-CSDS (some editions with Tata Trusts, Lal Family Foundation)
geo_coverage: varies by edition; 2019 covered 20+ states, 2020-21 covered 11 conflict-affected states
caveats: PERCEPTION and self-report, not incidence - must never be rendered as a crime measure
sample frames differ radically between editions (police personnel vs households vs both), so editions are not a time series
2020-21 edition is restricted to conflict-affected states and is not nationally representative
results published as PDF narrative; underlying survey data not released as open microdata
evidence: Editions confirmed from fetched content. A news corpus file (k-wal/farmers-movement-archive, deccanherald 24-08-2021) describes 'Status of Policing in India Report 2020-2021: Policing in Conflict-Affected Regions' by Common Cause with CSDS, Lokniti, Tata Trusts and Lal Family Foundation, surveying 11 states (J&K, AP, Telangana, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Bihar, Assam, Tripura, Nagaland, Manipur), and quotes findings (21% of police and 19% of public endorse killing a dangerous Naxalite over legal trial; 22% knew a woman arrested/detained). A fetched link-audit file (dyrok/sih-hackathon-26) records SPIR 2019 'Police Adequacy and Working Conditions' as a survey of 11,834 police across 20+ states and commoncause.in as live HTTP 200. SPIR 2023 referenced in IM-GPT/nyaysetu-delhi-police-voice-copilot docs as covering citizen trust, perceptions of bias and support for violence.
how_to_obtain: commoncause.in -> Publications. PDFs are free.
notes: Use for a clearly-separated 'trust in police' tab. Its real analytical value is explaining WHY registration is low in a given state, not measuring crime.

name: India Justice Report
publisher: India Justice Report consortium (Tata Trusts-initiated; with CHRI, Common Cause, CSDS, DAKSH, TISS-Prayas, Vidhi)
time_latest: 2022 (a 2025 edition is referenced elsewhere, unconfirmed here)
license: unstated (a third-party catalogue claims free-for-non-commercial-with-attribution; unverified)
caveats: measures justice-system CAPACITY, not crime - no incidence, no victimisation
state level only, no district breakdown
built entirely from official returns (DPO, PSI, NJDG, NALSA), so it inherits their gaps
UTs and AFSPA states are scored but deliberately excluded from the ranking
self-described as 'limited by the unavailability and paucity of data and its inconsistencies'
evidence: Fetched the report site's own application source, frappe/ijr, including ijr/www/_methodology.md, ijr/www/rankings.py, ijr/www/state.py and the state_ranking doctype. 2022 edition: 102 indicators - police 30, prisons 29, judiciary 28, legal aid 15 - across six themes (Infrastructure, Human Resources, Diversity, Budgets, Workload, Trends), plus a standalone State Human Rights Commission pillar scored separately and excluded from the overall ranking. Sources per pillar: Data on Police Organizations 2022 (as at 1 Jan 2022); Prison Statistics India 2021 (as at 31 Dec 2021); NJDG/Supreme Court/Court News/DoJ 2022-23; NALSA 2020-21 to 2022; CAG documents and state budgets 2020-21. Clusters: I = 18 large/mid states (10M+), II = 7 small states, III = 8 UTs (unranked), IV = 3 AFSPA states (unranked). Code confirms rank fields for overall, police, prisons, judiciary, legal_aid, hr, diversity, trends.
how_to_obtain: open-download
notes: Best used as a credibility modifier on the map: poor police-capacity scores should widen the stated uncertainty on that state's registration counts.

name: Absence of a national crime victimisation survey for India (documented negative finding)
caveats: this is an absence, established by searching and not finding - it cannot be proved, only supported
NFHS covers intimate-partner and sexual violence only; it is not a general crime victimisation survey
BPR&D may have commissioned one-off victimisation studies that are poorly indexed online
evidence: No recurring Indian equivalent of the US NCVS or the England & Wales CSEW was found. The only national experienced-violence prevalence figures located are NFHS's, restricted to intimate-partner and sexual violence. The nearest general-crime victimisation instrument found is the one-off IDFC Institute SATARC multi-city survey. Search capacity for this session was limited (WebSearch budget exhausted after two queries), so this should be re-tested before publication.
how_to_obtain: n/a - publish as methodology content
notes: PUBLISHABLE FINDING. It is the reason every district colour on this map is a statement about police records rather than about safety, and it belongs on the methodology page in those words.

name: SATARC - Safety Trends and Reporting of Crime (multi-city victimisation survey)
caveats: one-off, dated, four cities only - no national or district coverage
city-level results; sub-city breakdown unknown
if microdata is not released, only published aggregate reporting rates are usable
evidence: Not verified in this session - no URL fetched. Recorded from prior knowledge as the nearest thing India has to a city crime victimisation survey, explicitly designed to measure the gap between crimes experienced and crimes registered. All candidate domains were egress-blocked and WebSearch budget was exhausted.
how_to_obtain: Search the IDFC Institute publications archive; if the institute has wound down, look for the working paper in an institutional repository or contact the named authors directly.
notes: If the offence-wise reporting rates can be obtained this becomes the best available basis for per-category under-registration multipliers - exactly the number the map needs for honest confidence language. Verify before relying on it.

name: India Human Development Survey (IHDS)
publisher: NCAER with University of Maryland (Sonalde Desai, Reeve Vanneman)
caveats: NOT district-representative - district identifiers exist but sub-state estimates are unreliable
crime and policing are not headline topics; safety content is incidental (confidence in institutions, household conflict)
panel design means attrition between waves
evidence: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India_Human_Development_Survey (fetched 2026-09-19): three waves - 2004-05, 2011-12, 2022-23; wave 1 covered 41,554 households in 1,503 villages and 971 urban neighbourhoods; later waves re-interviewed 37,000+ plus refreshers; NIH-funded; site ihds.umd.edu. Topic list given as health, education, employment, economic status, marriage, fertility, gender relations and social capital - crime/safety NOT named. ICPSR archiving not confirmed by the article.
how_to_obtain: Register at ICPSR and download the IHDS study; or request via ihds.umd.edu.
notes: Worth one pass over the questionnaire to see whether the confidence-in-police and household-conflict items are usable as a secondary perception layer. Low priority relative to NFHS.

name: NSSO / NSS rounds touching safety (negative finding)
caveats: no NSS round is a crime victimisation survey
safety-adjacent content (lighting, transport, mobility, amenities) is incidental and is not an incidence measure
published below state x sector only rarely
evidence: No NSS crime victimisation module was identified. Recorded as a negative finding so the search is not repeated. Not independently verified in this session (mospi.gov.in not fetched; WebSearch budget exhausted).
how_to_obtain: mospi.gov.in round catalogue; microdata via MoSPI's data archive.
notes: Deprioritise unless a specific round is shown to carry a victimisation module.

name: Lok Foundation-Oxford University Surveys
publisher: Lok Foundation and University of Oxford, fieldwork by CMIE
caveats: PERCEPTION and attitudes only - no incidence
results published as newspaper articles and summaries rather than an open microdata series
rounds are not a consistent panel of questions
evidence: Not verified in this session - no URL fetched, no domain reachable. Recorded from prior knowledge as a nationally representative attitude survey carried on CMIE's field network, with rounds covering gender attitudes, institutional trust and public-space safety perception.
how_to_obtain: Contact Lok Foundation or the Oxford principal investigators; published summaries have historically appeared in Mint.
notes: Low priority. Perception data with no open microdata is close to unusable for a map.

name: CMIE Consumer Pyramids Household Survey
caveats: NO crime or victimisation module - income, consumption, employment and sentiment only
geography is CMIE's own 'homogeneous regions', which are not administrative districts
expensive; sampling design has been academically contested
evidence: Not fetched in this session. Catalogued from prior knowledge to close the loop: ~175k households at high frequency with genuinely fine geography, but no crime content.
how_to_obtain: Commercial subscription from CMIE.
notes: Explicitly NOT a crime source. Recorded so nobody spends budget on it expecting one.

name: Praja Foundation city reports (incl. state of policing and law & order)
geo_coverage: Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru and other cities
caveats: GRANULARITY CLAIM UNVERIFIED - the brief assumed ward-level crime; police RTI returns are organised by police station or police district, which do not map to municipal wards
ward-level Praja data is civic-complaint and councillor-performance data, not crime
RTI-derived, so coverage depends on what each authority chose to answer in a given year
published as PDF narrative and charts - expect table extraction, not a data download
evidence: praja.org returned EGRESS_BLOCKED from this session and no mirrored Praja data artefact was found on the reachable surfaces (GitHub code search for Praja returned only unrelated noise). The granularity statement in this record is my assessment from how Indian police RTI returns are structured, explicitly flagged as an assessment rather than a finding.
how_to_obtain: Open praja.org from an unblocked network; reports are free PDFs. If a report cites RTI replies, email Praja for the underlying RTI response set and methodology appendix. Failing that, file the same RTIs with Mumbai/Delhi police - the reports document which questions were asked.
notes: HIGHEST-PRIORITY UNVERIFIED ENTRY. If the policing reports really are police-station-level and annual, this is the finest-grained non-government crime data in India and should move to priority 5.

name: Annual Survey of India's City-Systems (ASICS)
publisher: Janaagraha Centre for Citizenship and Democracy
caveats: NOT a crime or safety measure - scores urban governance quality (laws, planning, capacity, transparency, participation)
no victimisation, no incidence, no policing outcomes
city level only
evidence: Not fetched in this session; janaagraha.org not reachable and GitHub code search returned nothing. Recorded from prior knowledge.
how_to_obtain: janaagraha.org -> publications.
notes: Context only. Do not represent ASICS scores as safety scores.

name: Open City - Urban Data Portal (data.opencity.in)
license: unknown (varies by dataset; most are republished GoI data)
caveats: a republisher, not a primary source - always trace to the original
holdings are uneven; Bengaluru coverage is much deeper than elsewhere
cleaned copies can silently diverge from the government original
evidence: A real resource URL of the form https://data.opencity.in/dataset/530ee93a-d24c-43df-b90b-272a067d5a4e/resource/f8095b22-bb15-470f-a0a8-6d21b982aa8a/download/uttar_pradesh-nhfs.pdf appeared in fetched search results, hosting an NFHS state factsheet. The domain itself returned EGRESS_BLOCKED when fetched directly.
how_to_obtain: open-download
notes: The dataset/<uuid>/resource/<uuid>/download/ URL structure is CKAN's. Try data.opencity.in/api/3/action/package_search?q=crime - if it responds, the whole catalogue is harvestable in one pass. This is the 'better-cleaned than the government original' category the brief asked for.

name: SHRUG - Socioeconomic High-resolution Rural-Urban Geographic Platform for India
license: open with attribution (confirm exact terms on the download page)
caveats: ACTUAL unit is the SHRUG 'shrid' (village/town), which has no exact match in this catalogue's granularity enum - recorded as 'ward' meaning 'finest sub-district administrative unit'
NOT a crime dataset - no crime, policing or victimisation content
its value is as a spatial spine: keys bridging Census, Economic Census, NSS, elections and nightlights across boundary changes
shrid keys must be mapped to police jurisdictions separately - police boundaries are not administrative boundaries
evidence: GitHub API search returned devdatalab/shrug-public: 'Issue tracking for the Socioeconomic High-resolution Rural-Urban Geographic Platform for India (SHRUG)', 35 stars, pushed_at 2026-08-17 - an actively maintained project. The download URL https://www.devdatalab.org/shrug_download/ was recovered from a fetched resource list (narayankishan/narayankishan.github.io resources.Rmd). devdatalab.org itself returned EGRESS_BLOCKED.
how_to_obtain: Email registration on the download page, then direct download.
notes: Ingest this early. District and sub-district boundary reconciliation across decades of reorganisation is a prerequisite for every other layer, and SHRUG is the standard solution.

name: Development Data Lab Judicial Data (e-Courts, 81.2 million cases)
license: open for research with attribution; extended (less anonymised) access on application
caveats: measures cases that REACHED COURT, not incidents and not FIRs - a third distinct quantity
ends 2018, so entirely pre-BNS (BNS/BNSS/BSA in force 1 July 2024)
e-Courts coverage and data quality vary sharply by state
act and section coding is inconsistent and needs normalisation before aggregation
fully anonymised - no addresses, no sub-district geography, no judge or litigant identity
district boundaries are as-recorded by each court, and need crosswalking
evidence: Verified from the Data Is Plural newsletter archive, edition 2021-02-24 (fetched via GitHub code search of data-is-plural/newsletter-archive), quoting: 'The Development Data Lab has gathered data on 81.2 million court cases in India's lower judiciary between 2010 and 2018, drawn from the country's e-Courts platform... the largest open-access dataset on judicial proceedings in the world... The public dataset contains each case's state, district, court, case type, filing and decision dates, defendant and petitioner genders, legal codes, and more. It has been fully anonymized to prevent the identification of individual judges or litigants, but researchers can apply for more extensive access.' Independently corroborated by apoorv74/ecourts-india-resources datasets.md: 'DDL Judicial Data Portal - This is a public dataset describing 81 million cases handled by the district courts in India from 2010-2018.' devdatalab.org was EGRESS_BLOCKED so the download itself was not opened.
how_to_obtain: open-download from devdatalab.org/judicial-data; apply to DDL for extended access.
notes: RECOMMENDED FIRST INGEST alongside NCRB. Gives a district x section x year series that is independent of NCRB's principal-offence rule, so it functions as a genuine cross-check on NCRB's category mix rather than an echo of it.

name: Justice Hub judicial datasets (POCSO, child labour, contract enforcement)
geo_coverage: Assam, Delhi, Haryana (POCSO); Assam, Bihar, Jharkhand, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, UP (child labour); ~29 states (contract enforcement)
license: unknown (open data platform; confirm per dataset)
caveats: court cases, not incidents
narrow act-specific slices, not general crime
three states only for POCSO - not a national series
derived from eCourts and inherits its per-state quality variation
evidence: Fetched apoorv74/ecourts-india-resources/datasets.md in full. It lists, with Justice Hub URLs: 'Unpacking Judicial Data to Track Implementation of the POCSO Act in Assam, Delhi & Haryana' - case details for the 19,783 cases registered in the district courts of those states, all downloaded from the eCourts portal; 'Analysis of Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986' - 10,800 cases from January 2015 to March 2023 across Assam, Bihar, Jharkhand, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh; and 'Data on Contract Enforcement Litigation' (NIPFP) covering five acts across court complexes in ~2 cities per state across 29 states. The catalogue was verified; individual dataset pages were not opened (justicehub.in not fetched).
how_to_obtain: open-download
notes: The POCSO archive is the most relevant: child sexual offence cases at district-court level with case detail, in a category where police registration is especially weak.

name: DAKSH judicial database
caveats: court cases, not incidents
dashboard-first presentation; bulk download availability unconfirmed
overlaps heavily with the DDL judicial dataset
evidence: Both URLs recovered from fetched content: apoorv74/ecourts-india-resources/datasets.md describes DAKSH's 'Deciphering Judicial Data' work cleaning and standardising eCourts case and hearing data, linking dakshindia.org/deciphering-judicial-data-daksha-database/; narayankishan/narayankishan.github.io resources.Rmd lists 'India High Courts Data | Daksh | https://database.dakshindia.org/'. Neither domain was fetched.
how_to_obtain: database.dakshindia.org; contact DAKSH for bulk extracts.
notes: Most useful as a CLEANING REFERENCE for the DDL judicial data - DAKSH's published work is precisely about normalising eCourts inconsistencies - rather than as a separate ingest.

name: pratapvardhan/NFHS-5 - machine-readable parse of NFHS-5 fact sheets
publisher: Pratap Vardhan (independent), published via Harvard Dataverse
geo_coverage: 341 districts across 21 states/UTs (NFHS-5 Phase 1); 36 states/UTs at state level
caveats: PHASE 1 ONLY - 341 of ~707 districts; Phase-2 states are missing
author's own warning: 'Quality checks have been minimally done. Please recheck with source before doing any analysis.'
NO violence indicators - 104 district indicators, none matching violence/empowerment/bank/mobile/decisions
district names are as printed in the factsheets and need crosswalking to Census or current district codes
evidence: Fetched the repo README and two data files. README: CSV fact sheets from NFHS 2019-20, source rchiips.org/nfhs/, NFHS-5-States.csv with 131 indicators across 28 states and 8 UTs, NFHS-5-Districts.csv covering 341 districts from 21 states, CC BY 4.0, DOI 10.7910/DVN/42WNZF, default branch master. Fetched NFHS-5-Districts.csv and counted the distinct Indicator values: exactly 104, numbered 1-104, ending '104. Men age 15 years and above who consume alcohol'; NO indicator contains 'violence' (also none containing empowerment/bank/mobile/decisions; the only 'menstrual' hit is indicator 19). Fetched district-level/NFHS-5-KL-Kerala.csv: header 'State,State-Code,District,Indicator,NFHS-5,NFHS-4,NFHS-5-note,NFHS-4-note', 1,040 rows, 14 Kerala districts, zero rows mentioning violence. Arithmetic cross-check: 341 x 104 = 35,464, exactly the district-file row count reported independently by kri6228/AnemiaFusionNet.
how_to_obtain: open-download
notes: THE EVIDENTIARY BASIS for this dossier's headline finding that NFHS-5 publishes no district-level violence data. Also carries the NFHS-4 value beside each NFHS-5 value, giving a built-in five-year trend. For full coverage seek the 698-district version documented by vybhav72954/trilytics_team_vector as NFHS5_district_factsheets_2019-21_long.csv.

name: SaiSiddhardhaKalla/NFHS - NFHS district parse with Census 2011 codes
caveats: the citing description is internally inconsistent - it claims '35,465 rows, 640 districts x ~104 indicators', but 640 x 104 = 66,560; 35,465 matches the 341-district Phase-1 count instead
unverified third-party parse with no stated QC
licence unknown - do not redistribute without checking
evidence: URL and description recovered from a fetched provenance file (chitagni/eco6810-final-project-template, peer-samples/03_literacy_imr_descriptive.md), which describes it as a 'third-party parse of the IIPS district factsheets (35,465 rows, 640 districts x ~104 indicators), with ST_CEN_CD and DT_CEN_CD Census 2011 codes attached'. The file itself was not fetched.
how_to_obtain: open-download
notes: The value here is NOT the indicators (which pratapvardhan's CC-BY version already provides) but the ST_CEN_CD / DT_CEN_CD Census 2011 code crosswalk, which is the join key to essentially every India district shapefile and saves a painful fuzzy-name-matching step. Verify row count and coverage before use.

name: Hindustan Times Labs - Women's Empowerment Index (NFHS-4)
caveats: a derived INDEX, not raw data - indicators are min-max rescaled, standardised and averaged
negative indicators are inverted so that higher always means better, which is exactly the transformation that misleads on a crime map if applied unthinkingly
NFHS-3 comparison available for only four indicators and 28 states/UTs
state level only
evidence: Fetched the README and data/103.csv. README: source NFHS round 4, 36 states/UTs, eight 'Women's Empowerment and Gender-Based Violence' indicators, methodology following an NIPFP governance-rating paper (rescale to 0-1, invert negatives, standardise, average), NFHS-3 comparison for four indicators across 28 states/UTs, licence not specified. data/103.csv header 'state,indicator,legend_name,urban,rural,total,rank' with indicator 103 = 'Ever-married women who have ever experienced spousal violence (%)' and full state values.
how_to_obtain: open-download
notes: Useful less as data than as a worked, citable precedent for the normalisation choices this project must make - including the direction-of-goodness trap.

name: Academic replication data - digitised NCRB district crime panels
publisher: various (AEA Data and Code Repository, Harvard Dataverse, ICPSR)
license: varies (most AEA/Dataverse deposits are open with attribution)
caveats: district boundaries are the paper's vintage, not current - reorganisation is unhandled
author-specific cleaning and imputation choices are baked in and often undocumented
usually a single crime head (e.g. crimes against women, dowry deaths) rather than the full NCRB taxonomy
reported-crime counts, inheriting NCRB's principal-offence rule and undercount
evidence: NO replication URL is asserted. Harvard Dataverse, Zenodo, arXiv and OpenAlex were all EGRESS_BLOCKED and the WebSearch budget was exhausted, so nothing in this category could be fetched. Recorded from prior knowledge of the literature: the canonical example is Iyer, Mani, Mishra & Topalova (AEJ: Applied, 2012) on women in local government and crime against women, which built a district-level NCRB panel and argued the observed increase reflected increased REPORTING rather than increased offending. Related strands: crime and rainfall/temperature shocks, dowry deaths, elections and violence.
how_to_obtain: Search the AEA Data and Code Repository by paper title first (deposits have been mandatory for AEA journals since ~2010), then Harvard Dataverse and ICPSR. Search terms: 'crime India district panel', 'crimes against women India district', 'dowry deaths district'.
notes: CHASE THIS BEFORE COMMISSIONING ANY OCR of NCRB district tables. The digitisation has very probably already been done and paid for by someone else, and this is potentially the largest single cost saving available to the project. Also note the Iyer et al. finding itself is directly usable as published evidence that rising recorded crime can mean better reporting - essential for the map's caveat language.

name: ACLED - Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Project (India)
license: ToU-restricts-reuse - free for non-commercial and academic use with registration and attribution; commercial use and redistribution are separately licensed
caveats: POLITICAL VIOLENCE AND PROTEST ONLY, not ordinary crime - riots, mob and communal violence, attacks on civilians, protests
media-sourced, so density tracks press attention and is biased toward English-language-covered areas
geo_precision 1/2/3 must be respected - 2 and 3 are approximate and sometimes only an admin centroid; never plot precision-3 events as exact points
India coverage starts 2016, later than the 2010 start for the rest of South/Southeast Asia - no pre-2016 backfill
event counts are not victim counts; the 'fatalities' field is a separate and often-revised estimate
records are revised retrospectively, so a re-pull changes history
evidence: acleddata.com returned EGRESS_BLOCKED. en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armed_Conflict_Location_and_Event_Data_Project (fetched 2026-09-19) states South and Southeast Asian countries are covered 'from 2010 to the present, with the exception of India (2016-present)'; that ACLED 'collects data in real time and releases updates on a weekly basis'; and that data 'can be downloaded from the website's Data Export Tool, the website's Curated Data Files, or directly from the ACLED API'. The record schema was corroborated across six independent fetched GitHub repositories (andybega/acledr, amy-deng/event-ctft, bradywilky/data_providers, thereseanders/workshop-dataviz-fsu, globalinteldesk01/intel-eye-map, BaileyM7/economic-warfare-osint) showing fields: event_id_cnty, event_date, year, time_precision, disorder_type, event_type, sub_event_type, actor1, assoc_actor_1, inter1, actor2, assoc_actor_2, inter2, interaction, civilian_targeting, region, country, admin1, admin2, admin3, location, latitude, longitude, geo_precision, source, source_scale, notes, fatalities, timestamp, iso3. The endpoint https://api.acleddata.com/acled/read with country/event_date/fields parameters and Bearer-token auth was seen in two of them.
how_to_obtain: Register at acleddata.com for an API key (free for non-commercial). Query country=India with an event_date range; use the fields= projection to limit payload. Confirm commercial/redistribution terms before publishing derived points.
notes: THE ONLY TRUE POINT-LEVEL LAYER in this domain. Ship it as its own toggle labelled 'political violence and protest', with a geo_precision filter, or it will be misread as a crime feed.

name: UNODC crime and criminal justice statistics (India)
publisher: United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime
caveats: NOT an independent measurement of India - India's submissions derive from NCRB, so UNODC inherits NCRB's undercount and principal-offence rule
the NCRB-head to ICCS mapping is lossy and changes over time
national only - no subnational breakdown for India
submission gaps mean the India series has holes
evidence: data.unodc.org returned EGRESS_BLOCKED from this session. Recorded from prior knowledge of UNODC's UN-CTS and homicide statistics programme; no page was opened, so the exact India series coverage is unconfirmed.
how_to_obtain: data.unodc.org / dataunodc.un.org - open download.
notes: Benchmarking only. Do NOT present as a cross-check on NCRB: it IS NCRB, reformatted.

name: WHO Global Health Estimates - interpersonal violence mortality (India)
caveats: MODELLED estimates built from vital registration and verbal autopsy, not counts - carry the uncertainty range
India's vital registration completeness and cause-of-death coverage are partial, so the model does heavy lifting
national only
homicide mortality is not 'murder cases registered' - the definitions differ
evidence: who.int not fetched in this session. Recorded from prior knowledge. The key claim - that WHO/GBD homicide estimates for India have historically diverged materially from NCRB murder counts - is asserted from prior knowledge and MUST be re-verified with actual numbers before it is published on the map.
how_to_obtain: who.int/data/global-health-estimates - open download.
notes: Genuinely INDEPENDENT of police records, which makes it the single most useful national-level sanity check available. Verify the divergence numbers before quoting them.

name: Global Burden of Disease - interpersonal violence, India state level
publisher: IHME, with the India State-Level Disease Burden Initiative (ICMR / PHFI / IHME)
caveats: MODELLED estimates with uncertainty intervals, not observed counts - a modelled state estimate must never be rendered with the same visual weight as an observed count
interpersonal violence deaths are a mortality concept, not a crime-registration concept
state level, no districts
heavily dependent on Indian vital-registration inputs of variable quality
evidence: ghdx.healthdata.org not fetched in this session (WebSearch budget exhausted; domain not attempted after repeated egress blocks). Recorded from prior knowledge that the India State-Level Disease Burden Initiative produces state-level cause-of-death estimates for India including interpersonal violence and self-harm.
how_to_obtain: GHDx results tool at ghdx.healthdata.org - select India, subnational, cause = interpersonal violence.
notes: The only police-independent violence measure available at STATE level for India. Pairs naturally with WHO GHE for a mortality-based cross-check on NCRB murder counts.

name: World Bank WDI - intentional homicides per 100,000 (SH.STA.HOMI.P5)
caveats: sourced from UNODC and therefore, for India, from NCRB - adds NO independent information
national only
indicator code should be confirmed before use; both VC.IHR.PSRC.P5 and SH.STA.HOMI.P5 appear in circulation for homicide series
evidence: Not fetched in this session. Recorded from prior knowledge; the exact indicator code is stated with low confidence and must be confirmed against the WDI catalogue before use.
how_to_obtain: WDI API - trivially accessible, no key required.
notes: Catalogued for completeness and international benchmarking. Low value: it is NCRB laundered through two intermediaries.

name: Global Peace Index (India)
caveats: a composite of composites - several inputs are themselves derived from NCRB, so it is not independent
blends conflict, militarisation and 'societal safety and security' into one score, which is not a crime measure
national only
year-on-year movements often reflect methodology or input changes rather than real change
evidence: Not fetched in this session. Recorded from prior knowledge.
how_to_obtain: economicsandpeace.org - free report download with registration.
notes: Catalogued mainly to explain why it should NOT be used. A composite index is the opposite of what this map needs.

name: IndiaSpend - data journalism and incident trackers
caveats: MEDIA-REPORT-DERIVED - counts events reported in the press, a fourth and narrower quantity than police-reported crime, with severe and non-random selection
English-language press bias
trackers have in the past been paused or taken down - archive anything relied upon
no denominator, so counts cannot be turned into rates
evidence: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IndiaSpend returned HTTP 404 and indiaspend.com was not reachable from this session. Recorded from prior knowledge that IndiaSpend built and maintained original incident databases from media reports, notably a hate-crime / cow-related-violence tracker with dates and locations.
how_to_obtain: indiaspend.com; check the Internet Archive for any tracker that has been taken down.
notes: Incident-level with dates and locations is rare and valuable, but the selection bias is severe. If used at all, present as 'incidents reported in national media', never as counts.

name: Factly / Dataful - Indian open data repository
caveats: a republisher - always trace back to the government original
freemium: some datasets are paid, and terms may forbid building a public product on them
cleaning choices are not always documented, so figures can silently diverge from the source
district-level NCRB coverage is CLAIMED, not confirmed
evidence: dataful.in and factly.in were not reachable from this session and GitHub code search for both domains returned zero results. Recorded from prior knowledge that Factly runs a large Indian open-data repository (Dataful, formerly Factly DataSets) republishing government datasets including NCRB series in machine-readable, API-accessible form.
how_to_obtain: Open dataful.in, search 'NCRB' / 'Crime in India', check whether district tables are present and at what pricing tier. CONFIRM REDISTRIBUTION RIGHTS IN WRITING before building a public map on it.
notes: BEST CHEAP-WIN LEAD. If Dataful already holds NCRB district tables as clean CSV, it removes a large part of this project's hardest ingestion work. Verify early - the licence question is the blocker, not the data.

name: Article-14, Scroll.in and The Hindu data team - criminal justice datasets
caveats: published as narrative with an accompanying table, not as a maintained dataset
hand-assembled databases with undocumented inclusion criteria
copyright: news content is not reusable by default - get permission or use only as a pointer
paywalls on some outlets
evidence: No outlet page was fetched in this session. Recorded from prior knowledge that Article-14 in particular has published case-level databases on undertrials, sedition/UAPA prosecutions and police accountability, assembled by hand.
how_to_obtain: Read the investigation, then request the underlying data from the newsroom, or reconstruct it from the official records the piece cites.
notes: Treat as LEADS TO UNDERLYING OFFICIAL RECORDS, not as sources in their own right. Their main value is telling you which RTI to file.

name: Police Data Accessibility Project and Vera Police Data Transparency Index (methodological precedent, USA)
publisher: Police Data Accessibility Project; Vera Institute of Justice
geo_coverage: USA (out of geographic scope - precedent only)
caveats: USA only - no India content whatsoever
included purely as a design precedent for this project's own catalogue and credibility scoring
evidence: Fetched the Data Is Plural newsletter archive, edition 2024-01-24, which states: PDAP 'is compiling a meta-dataset of police records: where to find them online, what time period they cover, how often they're updated, and other characteristics', with a searchable and downloadable dataset of 1,700+ resources including traffic stop datasets, crime maps and use-of-force reports across hundreds of agencies, plus a dataset of 23,000+ criminal legal agencies; and that Vera's Police Data Transparency Index 'scored 90+ local police agencies across 10 categories of data transparency', with a downloadable methodology spreadsheet.
how_to_obtain: open-download
notes: PDAP's per-source schema is close to exactly what this project's Phase 1 is building, and Vera's transparency scoring is a ready-made model for the per-state credibility rating this map will need. Borrow both.

name: Community dataset catalogues for Indian crime and policing
caveats: awesome-datasets' quantitative metadata is NOT credible - it asserts figures like '~2 GB per edition' for NCRB Crime in India and '~500 MB' for the India Justice Report, and reads as machine-generated
several 'research' repos encountered during this work are LLM-written and confidently wrong; do not cite them as evidence
apoorv74/ecourts-india-resources is hand-curated and was reliable in every checkable respect
evidence: Fetched apoorv74/ecourts-india-resources/datasets.md in full - accurate, hand-curated, five judicial datasets with correct descriptions and working-looking URLs. Also saw connu/awesome-datasets topics/crime-and-policing/README.md and in/dataset-02.json via code search: it lists NCRB Crime in India (https://www.ncrb.gov.in/crime-in-india.html, GODL-India), NCRB Prison Statistics India (https://www.ncrb.gov.in/prison-statistics-india.html), India Justice Report (https://indiajusticereport.org/) and the data.gov.in public-safety sector page (https://www.data.gov.in/sector/public-safety-law-and-justice), each with format and licence metadata - but with implausible size figures.
how_to_obtain: open-download
notes: HARVEST THE URLS, DISCARD THE METADATA. Re-derive every field independently. Noted here mainly as a warning: a lot of the India-crime 'catalogue' content now on GitHub is LLM-generated and internally inconsistent, and this dossier's own hard rule against unverified URLs exists for exactly that reason.
